title: Vue 3 Migration for model-vue Library with Parallel Agent Approach

context.problem: Vue 2 reached End of Life on December 31, 2023. The model-vue library requires migration to Vue 3 to support modern apps, receive security updates, and maintain long-term viability.
constraints: model-vue is a library consumed by multiple applications (pqs-frontend, pqs-mobile, future apps)
Breaking changes affect all consumers simultaneously
Must coordinate migration with all consuming apps
Cannot break consuming apps during migration
2+ years past Vue 2 EOL (critical security risk)
requirements: Support both Vue 2 and Vue 3 versions
Complete migration within 6-8 weeks using parallel agents

alternatives_considered.name: Big Bang Migration
alternatives_considered.rejected_reason: Too risky for library - breaks all consumers immediately with no rollback

alternatives_considered.name: Compatibility Build (@vue/compat)
alternatives_considered.rejected_reason: Technical debt, performance penalty, larger bundle, temporary solution

alternatives_considered.name: Rewrite from Scratch
alternatives_considered.rejected_reason: Too expensive (6-12 months), reintroduces bugs, loses institutional knowledge

alternatives_considered.name: Stay on Vue 2 Forever
alternatives_considered.rejected_reason: EOL security risk, ecosystem abandonment, can't hire Vue 2 developers

alternatives_considered.name: Sequential AI-Assisted Migration
alternatives_considered.rejected_reason: Takes 12-15 weeks vs 6-8 weeks with parallel approach

decision: Adopt AI-assisted migration with junior developer supervision and CTO oversight. Use Cursor Ultra parallel subagents for code generation, junior developer for daily review and testing (20 hrs/week), and CTO for strategic decisions (8 hrs/week). Maintain both Vue 2 (v0.x) and Vue 3 (v1.x) versions during 11-week migration covering both model-vue library and pqs-frontend application. Use monorepo structure, Vite build system, Composition API, TypeScript, and tree-shakeable exports. Timeline: 6 weeks library + 5 weeks frontend with overlap.
consequences: POSITIVE: 91% cost reduction ($24K vs $280K manual), eliminates CRITICAL security risk (2+ years unpatched), modern ecosystem access, junior developer upskills in Vue 3, CTO maintains strategic oversight, AI handles 80% of code generation. Completes both library and frontend migration in 11-13 weeks. NEGATIVE: Slightly longer timeline than full senior dev approach, requires CTO time commitment (8 hrs/week), junior dev learning curve, short-term dual version maintenance. RISKS: See RA-000002 for Vue 2 continuation risk, RA-000003 for migration execution risks.
guardrails: All 9 components must have >80% test coverage before considered complete
Daily senior dev review and merge cycle required for agent outputs
No breaking changes to existing Vue 2 API without deprecation warning
Alpha/beta testing with pqs-frontend required before stable release
Maintain Vue 2 version for minimum 12 months after Vue 3 stable release
All agents must follow patterns defined in .cursor/MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md
Integration tests with both Vuex and Pinia adapters required

risk.rationale: Medium risk. Junior developer may miss subtle issues, but mitigated by CTO oversight on critical decisions and AI-generated code quality. Library nature means bugs affect multiple consumers. Mitigated by: comprehensive testing (>80% coverage), alpha/beta releases, maintaining Vue 2 fallback, daily junior dev review, CTO approval on key decisions, and AI parallel subagents reducing human error.

review.human: Pending - requires senior Vue developer and stakeholder approval. Parallel agent approach is innovative and significantly reduces cost/timeline compared to manual or sequential approaches.
